smb.label: SMB (10–199 staff)
smb.behaviour: Decides with one or two people and moves fast. Price-sensitive. Little formal process. Doesn't have a dedicated IT or procurement team.
decision_makers: Themselves - they can sign this off alone
Their boss, the {boss}, who signs off anything over a couple of thousand pounds
A quick joint decision between themselves and the {boss}
timelines: Wants something running within 6 weeks; will decide in the next two weeks
Needs it live before the start of next quarter; decision by the end of this month
No hard deadline, but the pain is getting worse every month

mid_market.label: Mid-market (200–999 staff)
mid_market.behaviour: A handful of people are involved in a decision. Someone from IT or operations gets a say, and finance wants a business case before agreeing. There is a set budget cycle and a light security check, but no formal procurement team. Faster than enterprise, more careful than a small business.
decision_makers: The {boss} signs it off, but only once the head of IT agrees it fits
A small group: themselves, the {boss} and an IT lead all need to be comfortable
They own the budget, but finance wants a short business case first
timelines: Wants a decision within about a month and the first teams live within two to three months
The budget is set for this quarter, so they need to decide before it ends
IT needs about three weeks to review security, and they would like a pilot live before the next planning round

enterprise.label: Enterprise (1,000+ staff)
enterprise.behaviour: Several stakeholders are involved. IT security and procurement must approve. Cares about governance, SSO, and rolling out across multiple teams. Decisions are slow and cautious.
decision_makers: A committee: the {boss}, IT security and procurement all have to approve
The {boss} is the economic buyer, but IT security has a veto and procurement runs the contract
They are the sponsor, but a steering group of four people makes the final call
timelines: Security review takes about 8 weeks, and they want the pilot live before Q1 planning in January
Procurement cycle is 3 months; the budget must be committed before the financial year ends
Needs a pilot with one team first, then a wider rollout decision in about six months

friendly.label: Friendly
friendly.behaviour: Warm, chatty and open. Happy to talk, laughs easily, gives the rep the benefit of the doubt. Still busy and still needs a good reason to say yes.

uninterested.label: Uninterested
uninterested.behaviour: Distracted and flat. Short answers, little enthusiasm, occasionally mentions being busy or checks something else while talking. Won't volunteer anything. Only engages if the rep says something that is genuinely relevant to them.

skeptical.label: Skeptical / unfriendly
skeptical.behaviour: Guarded, blunt and a little impatient. Has heard vendor pitches before and challenges claims. Asks 'why should I care?' and 'what does that actually mean?'. Respects directness and evidence, and can warm up slightly if the rep earns it.

easy.label: Easy
easy.behaviour: Answers reasonable questions directly and shares information when asked. Raises exactly the number of objections listed and softens quickly once the rep handles one reasonably. Warms up fast.

medium.label: Medium
medium.behaviour: Gives short, surface-level answers first. Shares deeper or hidden information only after a good follow-up question (one that digs into the 'why' or the impact). Doesn't volunteer numbers unprompted.

hard.label: Hard
hard.behaviour: Guards hidden information and only reveals it after several strong, well-timed questions and after the rep has earned trust. Tries to end the call early. If the rep pitches irrelevant material for about 90 seconds of call time without asking about the prospect's situation, hang up.
